correctness.rationale: Every dual cross-Gramian is precisely an idempotent projection onto \(W=\operatorname{ran}F^*=z^\perp\), hence has the unique form \(G=I-qz^*\) with \(z^*q=1\). Its off-diagonal objective is \(\max_i b_i|q_i|\). The inequality \(1=|z^*q|\le\sum_i|z_i||q_i|\le\mu\sum_i a_i/b_i\) gives the stated lower bound. Equality forces every \(b_i|q_i|\) to equal \(\mu_*\) and all \(\overline z_iq_i\) to have common nonnegative phase, yielding the unique optimizer. The canonical projection is \(I-zz^*/\|z\|^2\), so equality with the optimizer is equivalent to constant \(a_i b_i\). The exact-rational verifier independently confirms the displayed counterexample, both dual identities and coherences \(2/5<3/7\).

final_claim: Every full-spark excess-one frame in \(\mathbb C^n\) has a unique Grassmannian dual for the maximal off-diagonal cross-coherence objective; the optimizer is given by the stated kernel-coordinate formula and is canonical exactly when \(|z_i|\max_{j\ne i}|z_j|\) is constant. The displayed real \(2\times3\) frame has a unique noncanonical optimizer of coherence \(2/5\), while its canonical dual has coherence \(3/7\).
limitations: Full-spark frames with exactly one vector of excess only.
